title: How Did the Door Gods Come About?
synopsis: Menshen, or door gods, are divine protectors of doors and gates in Chinese folk religion, warding off evil influences and inviting positive ones.

fullText.simplified:
门神是怎么来的？

    你有没有注意过，春节的时候，有些人会在大门上贴画？画里的人穿着古代的衣服，样子威严。这就是“门神”。中国人相信，“门神”可以守护家门，不让鬼怪和坏人进来。这个习俗，其实有着很长的历史。
    很久以前，人们相信世界上有鬼，也怕它们半夜闯进来。所以，最早的门神是捉鬼的神仙。那时候的门是两扇开的，人们就在左右两扇门上各贴一位门神。于是，门神成双成对地出现，就成了固定的传统。
    后来，人们不只想把坏东西挡在门外，也希望好运能走进家门。于是到了宋朝，有了“文门神”。这类门神看起来性格温和，很好相处。他们代表人们对幸福、健康、财富的愿望。
    到了明清时期，门神的形象又发生了变化。那时候小说和戏剧很流行，人们爱去茶馆听书。书里讲了一个关于唐朝皇帝李世民的故事：他说自己因为兄弟相争的事，常在夜里做噩梦，梦到很多恶鬼来抓他。后来他让两位武将站在卧室门外，就再也不做噩梦了。于是，明朝人开始把武将也画出来贴在门上。
    到了当代，大部分房子的大门由两扇变成了一扇，贴门神的人越来越少了。如果想看到门神画像，可能要去乡村看看。在一些乡村，老人们还保留着贴门神的习俗。
    虽然门神的样子变了、贴门神的人少了，但人们希望守护家的心情并没有变。如果让人随便进出自己家的家门，一定会带来很多麻烦。学会合理的拒绝，才能给自己一个理想的家。在今天，保护家的方式不再是贴画，而是学会说“不”，懂得拒绝不合适的人。某种意义上，拒绝的技巧，就是当代人的门神。
fullText.traditional:
門神是怎麼來的？

    你有沒有注意過，春節的時候，有些人會在大門上貼畫？畫裡的人穿著古代的衣服，樣子威嚴。這就是“門神”。中國人相信，“門神”可以守護家門，不讓鬼怪和壞人進來。這個習俗，其實有著很長的歷史。
    很久以前，人們相信世界上有鬼，也怕牠們半夜闖進來。所以，最早的門神是捉鬼的神仙。那時候的門是兩扇開的，人們就在左右兩扇門上各貼一位門神。於是，門神成雙成對地出現，就成了固定的傳統。
    後來，人們不只想把壞東西擋在門外，也希望好運能走進家門。於是到了宋朝，有了“文門神”。這類門神看起來性格溫和，很好相處。他們代表人們對幸福、健康、財富的願望。
    到了明清時期，門神的形象又發生了變化。那時候小說和戲劇很流行，人們愛去茶館聽書。書裡講了一個關於唐朝皇帝李世民的故事：他說自己因為兄弟相爭的事，常在夜裡做噩夢，夢到很多惡鬼來抓他。後來他讓兩位武將站在臥室門外，就再也不做噩夢了。於是，明朝人開始把武將也畫出來貼在門上。
    到了當代，大部分房子的大門由兩扇變成了一扇，貼門神的人越來越少了。如果想看到門神畫像，可能要去鄉村看看。在一些鄉村，老人們還保留著貼門神的習俗。
    雖然門神的樣子變了、貼門神的人少了，但人們希望守護家的心情並沒有變。如果讓人隨便進出自己家的家門，一定會帶來很多麻煩。學會合理的拒絕，才能給自己一個理想的家。在今天，保護家的方式不再是貼畫，而是學會說“不”，懂得拒絕不合適的人。某種意義上，拒絕的技巧，就是當代人的門神。

sentences.simplified: 画里的人穿着古代的衣服，样子威严。这就是“门神”。
sentences.traditional: 畫裡的人穿著古代的衣服，樣子威嚴。這就是“門神”。
sentences.pinyin: huà lǐ de rén chuān zhe gǔ dài de yī fu yàng zi wēi yán zhè jiù shì mén shén
sentences.english: Have you ever noticed that during the Spring Festival, some people paste images on their front doors?

sentences.simplified: 中国人相信，“门神”可以守护家门，不让鬼怪和坏人进来。
sentences.traditional: 中國人相信，“門神”可以守護家門，不讓鬼怪和壞人進來。
sentences.pinyin: zhōng guó rén xiāng xìn mén shén kě yǐ shǒu hù jiā mén bú ràng guǐ guài hé huài rén jìn lái
sentences.english: The figures in the images are dressed in ancient clothing and have a dignified appearance. These are the “door gods.”

sentences.simplified: 这个习俗，其实有着很长的历史。
sentences.traditional: 這個習俗，其實有著很長的歷史。
sentences.pinyin: zhè ge xí sú qí shí yǒu zhe hěn cháng de lì shǐ
sentences.english: Chinese people believe that “door gods” can protect the home and prevent evil forces and bad people from entering.
This custom actually has a long history.

sentences.simplified: 很久以前，人们相信世界上有鬼，也怕它们半夜闯进来。
sentences.traditional: 很久以前，人們相信世界上有鬼，也怕牠們半夜闖進來。
sentences.pinyin: hěn jiǔ yǐ qián rén men xiāng xìn shì jiè shang yǒu guǐ yě pà tā men bàn yè chuǎng jìn lái

sentences.simplified: 所以，最早的门神是捉鬼的神仙。
sentences.traditional: 所以，最早的門神是捉鬼的神仙。
sentences.pinyin: suǒ yǐ zuì zǎo de mén shén shì zhuō guǐ de shén xiān
sentences.english: A long time ago, people believed that there were ghosts in the world and were afraid they would break in in the middle of the night.

sentences.simplified: 那时候的门是两扇开的，人们就在左右两扇门上各贴一位门神。
sentences.traditional: 那時候的門是兩扇開的，人們就在左右兩扇門上各貼一位門神。
sentences.pinyin: nà shí hou de mén shì liǎng shàn kāi de rén men jiù zài zuǒ yòu liǎng shàn mén shang gè tiē yí wèi mén shén
sentences.english: Therefore, the earliest door gods were deities who captured ghosts.

sentences.simplified: 于是，门神成双成对地出现，就成了固定的传统。
sentences.traditional: 於是，門神成雙成對地出現，就成了固定的傳統。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì mén shén chéng shuāng chéng duì de chū xiàn jiù chéng le gù dìng de chuán tǒng
sentences.english: At that time, doors had two panels, and people would paste a door god on each of the left and right panels.
As a result, door gods appeared in pairs, becoming an established tradition.

sentences.simplified: 后来，人们不只想把坏东西挡在门外，也希望好运能走进家门。
sentences.traditional: 後來，人們不只想把壞東西擋在門外，也希望好運能走進家門。
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái rén men bù zhǐ xiǎng bǎ huài dōng xi dǎng zài mén wài yě xī wàng hǎo yùn néng zǒu jìn jiā mén

sentences.simplified: 于是到了宋朝，有了“文门神”。
sentences.traditional: 於是到了宋朝，有了“文門神”。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì dào le sòng cháo yǒu le wén mén shén
sentences.english: Later, people not only wanted to keep bad things out but also hoped for good fortune to enter their homes.

sentences.simplified: 这类门神看起来性格温和，很好相处。
sentences.traditional: 這類門神看起來性格溫和，很好相處。
sentences.pinyin: zhè lèi mén shén kàn qǐ lái xìng gé wēn hé hěn hǎo xiāng chǔ
sentences.english: As a result, “civil door gods” emerged during the Song Dynasty.

sentences.simplified: 他们代表人们对幸福、健康、财富的愿望。
sentences.traditional: 他們代表人們對幸福、健康、財富的願望。
sentences.pinyin: tā men dài biǎo rén men duì xìng fú jiàn kāng cái fù de yuàn wàng
sentences.english: These types of door gods appear gentle in nature and easy to get along with.
They represent people’s wishes for happiness, health, and wealth.

sentences.simplified: 到了明清时期，门神的形象又发生了变化。
sentences.traditional: 到了明清時期，門神的形象又發生了變化。
sentences.pinyin: dào le míng qīng shí qī mén shén de xíng xiàng yòu fā shēng le biàn huà

sentences.simplified: 那时候小说和戏剧很流行，人们爱去茶馆听书。
sentences.traditional: 那時候小說和戲劇很流行，人們愛去茶館聽書。
sentences.pinyin: nà shí hou xiǎo shuō hé xì jù hěn liú xíng rén men ài qù chá guǎn tīng shū
sentences.english: By the Ming and Qing dynasties, the image of door gods underwent another transformation.

sentences.simplified: 书里讲了一个关于唐朝皇帝李世民的故事：
sentences.traditional: 書裡講了一個關於唐朝皇帝李世民的故事：
sentences.pinyin: shū lǐ jiǎng le yí ge guān yú táng cháo huáng dì lǐ shì mín de gù shi
sentences.english: At that time, novels and dramas were very popular, and people loved going to teahouses to listen to storytelling.

sentences.simplified: 他说自己因为兄弟相争的事，常在夜里做噩梦，
sentences.traditional: 他說自己因為兄弟相爭的事，常在夜裡做噩夢，
sentences.pinyin: tā shuō zì jǐ yīn wèi xiōng dì xiāng zhēng de shì cháng zài yè li zuò è mèng
sentences.english: A book tells a story about Emperor Li Shimin of the Tang Dynasty.

sentences.simplified: 梦到很多恶鬼来抓他。
sentences.traditional: 夢到很多惡鬼來抓他。
sentences.pinyin: mèng dào hěn duō è guǐ lái zhuā tā
sentences.english: He said that because of a conflict with his brothers, he often had nightmares at night, ..

sentences.simplified: 后来他让两位武将站在卧室门外，就再也不做噩梦了。
sentences.traditional: 後來他讓兩位武將站在臥室門外，就再也不做噩夢了。
sentences.pinyin: hòu lái tā ràng liǎng wèi wǔ jiàng zhàn zài wò shì mén wài jiù zài yě bú zuò è mèng le
sentences.english: .. dreaming of many evil spirits coming to capture him.

sentences.simplified: 于是，明朝人开始把武将也画出来贴在门上。
sentences.traditional: 於是，明朝人開始把武將也畫出來貼在門上。
sentences.pinyin: yú shì míng cháo rén kāi shǐ bǎ wǔ jiàng yě huà chu lai tiē zài mén shang
sentences.english: Later, he had two military generals stand outside his bedroom door, and he no longer had nightmares.
As a result, people in the Ming Dynasty began to paint military generals and paste them on doors.

sentences.simplified: 到了当代，大部分房子的大门由两扇变成了一扇，贴门神的人越来越少了。
sentences.traditional: 到了當代，大部分房子的大門由兩扇變成了一扇，貼門神的人越來越少了。
sentences.pinyin: dào le dāng dài dà bù fen fáng zi de dà mén yóu liǎng shàn biàn chéng le yí shàn tiē mén shén de rén yuè lái yuè shǎo le

sentences.simplified: 如果想看到门神画像，可能要去乡村看看。
sentences.traditional: 如果想看到門神畫像，可能要去鄉村看看。
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ xiǎng kàn dào mén shén huà xiàng kě néng yào qù xiāng cūn kàn kan
sentences.english: In contemporary times, the front doors of most houses have changed from two panels to one, and fewer people are pasting door gods.

sentences.simplified: 在一些乡村，老人们还保留着贴门神的习俗。
sentences.traditional: 在一些鄉村，老人們還保留著貼門神的習俗。
sentences.pinyin: zài yì xiē xiāng cūn lǎo rén men hái bǎo liú zhe tiē mén shén de xí sú
sentences.english: If you want to see images of door gods, you might need to visit the countryside.
In some villages, the elderly still maintain the custom of pasting door gods.

sentences.simplified: 虽然门神的样子变了、贴门神的人少了，
sentences.traditional: 雖然門神的樣子變了、貼門神的人少了，
sentences.pinyin: suī rán mén shén de yàng zi biàn le tiē mén shén de rén shǎo le

sentences.simplified: 但人们希望守护家的心情并没有变。
sentences.traditional: 但人們希望守護家的心情並沒有變。
sentences.pinyin: dàn rén men xī wàng shǒu hù jiā de xīn qíng bìng méi yǒu biàn
sentences.english: Although the appearance of the door gods has changed and fewer people are pasting door gods, ..

sentences.simplified: 如果让人随便进出自己家的家门，一定会带来很多麻烦。
sentences.traditional: 如果讓人隨便進出自己家的家門，一定會帶來很多麻煩。
sentences.pinyin: rú guǒ ràng rén suí biàn jìn chū zì jǐ jiā de jiā mén yí dìng huì dài lái hěn duō má fan
sentences.english: .. people’s desire to protect their homes has not changed.

sentences.simplified: 学会合理的拒绝，才能给自己一个理想的家。
sentences.traditional: 學會合理的拒絕，才能給自己一個理想的家。
sentences.pinyin: xué huì hé lǐ de jù jué cái néng gěi zì jǐ yí ge lǐ xiǎng de jiā
sentences.english: If people were to allow anyone to come and go through their front door, it would definitely lead to a lot of trouble.

sentences.simplified: 在今天，保护家的方式不再是贴画，而是学会说“不”，懂得拒绝不合适的人。
sentences.traditional: 在今天，保護家的方式不再是貼畫，而是學會說“不”，懂得拒絕不合適的人。
sentences.pinyin: zài jīn tiān bǎo hù jiā de fāng shì bú zài shì tiē huà ér shì xué huì shuō bù dǒng de jù jué bù hé shì de rén
sentences.english: Learning to say no appropriately is essential for creating an ideal home for yourself.

sentences.simplified: 某种意义上，拒绝的技巧，就是当代人的门神。
sentences.traditional: 某種意義上，拒絕的技巧，就是當代人的門神。
sentences.pinyin: mǒu zhǒng yì yì shang jù jué de jì qiǎo jiù shì dāng dài rén de mén shén
sentences.english: Today, the way to protect your home is no longer by pasting images, but by learning to say “no” and knowing how to refuse unsuitable people.

sentence_translations: How Did the Door Gods Come About?
Have you ever noticed that during the Spring Festival, some people paste images on their front doors?
The figures in the images are dressed in ancient clothing and have a dignified appearance. These are the “door gods.”
Chinese people believe that “door gods” can protect the home and prevent evil forces and bad people from entering.
This custom actually has a long history.
A long time ago, people believed that there were ghosts in the world and were afraid they would break in in the middle of the night.
Therefore, the earliest door gods were deities who captured ghosts.
At that time, doors had two panels, and people would paste a door god on each of the left and right panels.
As a result, door gods appeared in pairs, becoming an established tradition.
Later, people not only wanted to keep bad things out but also hoped for good fortune to enter their homes.
As a result, “civil door gods” emerged during the Song Dynasty.
These types of door gods appear gentle in nature and easy to get along with.
They represent people’s wishes for happiness, health, and wealth.
By the Ming and Qing dynasties, the image of door gods underwent another transformation.
At that time, novels and dramas were very popular, and people loved going to teahouses to listen to storytelling.
A book tells a story about Emperor Li Shimin of the Tang Dynasty.
He said that because of a conflict with his brothers, he often had nightmares at night, ..
.. dreaming of many evil spirits coming to capture him.
Later, he had two military generals stand outside his bedroom door, and he no longer had nightmares.
As a result, people in the Ming Dynasty began to paint military generals and paste them on doors.
In contemporary times, the front doors of most houses have changed from two panels to one, and fewer people are pasting door gods.
If you want to see images of door gods, you might need to visit the countryside.
In some villages, the elderly still maintain the custom of pasting door gods.
Although the appearance of the door gods has changed and fewer people are pasting door gods, ..
.. people’s desire to protect their homes has not changed.
If people were to allow anyone to come and go through their front door, it would definitely lead to a lot of trouble.
Learning to say no appropriately is essential for creating an ideal home for yourself.
Today, the way to protect your home is no longer by pasting images, but by learning to say “no” and knowing how to refuse unsuitable people.
In a sense, the art of refusal is the door god of contemporary people.
